top_5_rigid_by_ratio.cell_type: enterocyte of epithelium of large intestine

stage2.verdict: No replication datasets support donor-split evolutionary ratio analysis

interpretation: Evolutionary ratio normalization (cross-species residual / within-species residual) was computed for 32 cell types across 100 donor splits. The ratio-normalized ranking shows low correlation with the raw residual ranking (Spearman ρ = 0.255), indicating that normalization substantially reshuffles type rankings. Ratios range from 0.56 to 4.35, with 17 types showing cross-species divergence more than 2× their within-species variation (ratio > 2) and 8 types showing divergence comparable to within-species noise (ratio < 1.5). Cross-atlas replication of ratio-normalized rankings could not be tested because no replication dataset (Sun2023, PanSci, CellHint) supports donor-split analysis — Sun2023 lacks donor metadata, PanSci data is in raw MTX format requiring prohibitive preprocessing, and CellHint/Census aggregates datasets with inconsistent donor tracking. The consensus ranking from raw residuals across 23 types identifies 5 stable types and 5 consistently extreme types, providing the most reliable characterization of cell type evolutionary rigidity despite the inability to test ratio normalization across atlases.
